summary: Runtime analysis was performed only through the approved isolated guest VM/x64dbg MCP workflow. The x64dbg MCP service was already reachable, so VM preparation was skipped per workflow. The sample loaded from C:\Users\h26v\Desktop\officecli.exe with ASLR base 0x00007FF7AA020000 and executed through the expected PE entry, CRT startup, TLS initialization gate, main, trace-writer assignment, and exe_start/hostfxr handoff breakpoints. Execution then stopped shortly after managed host startup. No persistence, injection, credential access, command-and-control domains, IPs, mutexes, or registry modifications were observed within the available observation window. Guest state was reverted to the clean VMRunV4 snapshot after analysis.

findings.title: Runtime confirms standard apphost startup path
findings.description: The live process hit the ASLR-adjusted entry, CRT, TLS gate, main, diagnostics writer setup, and exe_start addresses identified by static pass 1.
findings.reasoning: The observed breakpoint sequence matches the upstream static map and supports normal .NET apphost startup rather than a native unpacking shellcode path.

evidence.observation: module_get_main returned name officecli.exe, path C:\Users\h26v\Desktop\officecli.exe, base 0x00007FF7AA020000, entry 0x00007FF7AA5E6230, section_count 9, size 10080256.

Breakpoints were installed and hit at 0x00007FF7AA5E6230 (entry), 0x00007FF7AA5E6239 (CRT after cookie), 0x00007FF7AA5E6159 (TLS initialization gate), 0x00007FF7AA059D90 (main), 0x00007FF7AA059EC3 (trace writer assignment), and 0x00007FF7AA059070 (exe_start).

limitations: The run observed native startup and immediate host handoff only; managed-code internals were not instrumented in depth.

findings.title: No runtime anti-analysis gate blocked startup
findings.description: No failing debugger, timing, or gate-value check was encountered before the hostfxr/apphost handoff.
findings.reasoning: The sample progressed through all planned startup breakpoints without requiring branch or flag patching.

evidence.observation: debug_run advanced through the planned gate/startup breakpoints to exe_start and then into external runtime code without analyst patches to flags, branches, or gate values.

limitations: Absence of an observed gate in the native startup window does not rule out managed-code anti-analysis checks after hostfxr startup.

findings.title: No malicious runtime capabilities observed during window
findings.description: Persistence, injection, networking, and credential access were not observed during the available isolated debugger run.
findings.reasoning: The run focused on startup validation and did not surface API-resolver behavior, injected executable regions, network indicators, mutexes, or persistence artifacts before the process stopped.

sources.location: debug state and module/thread queries after run

evidence.observation: After the startup breakpoint sequence, debug_get_state returned state stopped; subsequent module_list returned an empty module list because the debugger was no longer attached to a running debuggee.
No domains, IP addresses, mutex names, registry keys, persistence locations, injection targets, or credential-access artifacts were observed during the debugger-controlled run.

limitations: No guest EDR/Procmon/packet-capture artifact was collected; findings are limited to x64dbg MCP observations and the short execution window.
